item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.7
item.description:
## A new Settings
Settings now has a sidebar of focused pages, like the one in System Settings, with Updates first.
- **Appearance:** choose Light, Dark or Auto for Resonance alone. Now Playing and Under the Hood stay dark in all three. - **Update channels:** choose Stable, Beta or Alpha in Settings → Updates. Alpha also gets betas. Your choice applies from the next release on. - **When an update fails:** Settings → Updates gives the real reason, with the details to copy for a bug report. An update that didn't install is noticed the next time Resonance opens.
## And more
- Playlists have a # column with each tune's place in the list. - A list sorted by a column has **Back to Original Order** above it, so a Top 100 keeps its ranking. - Installing the `resonance` command handles more setups: it avoids a folder where another program already has the name, tells you if your terminal may still run that program, and has a line to copy if the folder isn't on your PATH.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.6
item.description:
## A fresh start
This version is signed and notarized by Apple, so it opens like any other app, without a trip to Privacy & Security. It also runs in the App Sandbox, macOS's safe room for apps, and that means a fresh start: Resonance opens on Welcome again and doesn't see your old favourites, playlists or settings. Your earlier files are still in ~/Library/Application Support/Resonance. To keep the collection you already have, choose its HVSC folder there when Welcome asks, instead of downloading it again.
## Smart Playlists
Say what you'd like to hear, in your own words, and Resonance builds a playlist from all of HVSC by how each tune actually sounds.
## Resonance, from anywhere on your Mac
- Siri and Shortcuts: “Surprise me”, “Play something like this”, “Drift from this tune”, “Favourite this tune” and “Play Favourites”. - Spotlight finds the collection's tunes, and in Finder Space shows a SID file's title, composer and release. - The Dock icon shows a download's or scan's progress, and its menu has the controls. When Resonance is in the background, a finished download tells you. - The `resonance` command and its terminal app: playlists, search, Sounds Like, the tracker and full-screen visuals. Assistants such as Claude can use it too. Install it from Settings → Integrations. - A shared tune link now opens Resonance directly.
## And more
- Search is a place of its own: type from anywhere. - Under the Hood (⌥⌘U) slides up the tracker, registers and sweeps, every chip at once for multi-SID tunes. - Tunes outside HVSC get their length worked out, shown with a ~. - Now Playing shows the tune's fingerprint sphere. - Press ? for the keyboard shortcuts, with Vim and Emacs keys in Settings. - New credits: About Resonance → Credits.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.5
item.description:
## Scrub through a tune
Drag or click the progress bar, in the player bar, Now Playing or the menu bar player, and the tune goes there. Control Center's position slider and its 15-second skips work too.
A SID tune is a small C64 program, not a recording, so there's nothing to jump to: Resonance runs the tune to that point silently at about sixty times its speed. While it does, the bar shows where you're going in grey and the engine winding up to it, with the clock counting along; the sound comes back when it arrives, about a second per minute of tune on reSIDfp and less on SIDLite direct.
Scrubbing works on the reSIDfp and SIDLite direct engines. SIDLite and reSID play in real time only; a click on their bar says so.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.4
item.description:
## Two new sound engines
Resonance now plays through libsidplayfp, the emulator behind most SID players, rendered straight into the audio output.
- **reSIDfp** is the most accurate SID emulation available and is now the default. Tunes with filter sweeps and digi samples in particular sound closer to the real chip. - **SIDLite direct** is the same compact chip model as SIDLite, on the new player. It is the lightest on the processor of the four. - **SIDLite** and **reSID** are still there. Settings → Playback lists all four with a line on what sets each apart; changing the engine restarts the tune. - Widen mono tunes doesn't apply to the two new engines yet.
## Better Sounds Like
Sounds Like finds closer matches. In testing on composers it hadn't been tuned on, nearly twice as many of its suggestions came from the same composer as the tune you're playing.
- It now looks at how each instrument is shaped, not only which waveforms and effects a tune uses. - It also compares how tunes actually sound, using a small download made in advance. Nothing is analysed on your Mac beyond the usual scan. - Percentages in Sounds Like are worked out differently, so they won't match what you saw before. - Your fingerprints are rebuilt once: Resonance downloads the new set the first time you open it.
## Fixes
- Opening a tune from a nested composer folder, such as from Sounds Like, no longer shows an empty page with 0 tunes. It opens the folder the tune is listed under.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.3
item.description:
## Share a tune
Send a friend the tune you're listening to.
- **Share…** next to Add to… in Now Playing, the inspector and the menu bar player, and **Share** in a tune's right-click menu, makes a short link to any tune in HVSC: Copy Link, Messages, Mail, or any other app. - Pasted into Messages, Slack, Discord and the like, the link shows the tune's card: title, composer, year, length and its sound fingerprint. - A click on **Open in Resonance** opens the tune in Resonance, at the same subtune. If your collection is older and doesn't have it, Resonance offers the HVSC update; if you have no collection yet, the download. - Friends without Resonance get a page with the tune's card, its fingerprint turning, and a download link.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.2
item.description:
## Automatic updates
Resonance now keeps itself up to date.
- **Check for Updates…** in the Resonance menu looks for a new version right away. - Resonance checks once a day by itself. Turn this off, or let it download and install updates when you quit, in Settings → Advanced → Updates. - Every update is checked against Resonance's signing key before it's installed. Nothing about your Mac is sent.
This is the last version you need to download by hand.
